 Wedgewood pharmacy recalls compounded veterinary medications due to potency concerns
 Wedgewood Pharmacy is recalling several compounded veterinary medications that were shipped to pet owners, veterinary practices, and pharmacies over the last several months. The company is working to alert affected customers, provide refunds or replacements, and suggest clinical alternatives where appropriate.
 Emily Singler, VMD 
 Published Oct 23, 2026 
 Share
 facebook

 email 
 Advertisement
 Wedgewood Pharmacy announced a recall of certain veterinary compounded medications intended for use in companion, equine, exotic, zoo, wildlife, and aquatic species. This recall was initiated due to “inconsistencies in the reliability of certain analytical testing data generated by their laboratory,” according to an announcement issued by the company on October 21, 2026.
 These inconsistencies may have resulted in the production of subpotent and/or superpotent products, the announcement explained, noting that the company detected the inconsistencies through their own quality control processes.
 The affected products
 The affected medications were shipped throughout the U.S. between February 18, 2026, and October 6, 2026, to veterinary practices, pharmacies, and pet owners. A full list of affected products, which include powders, pastes, oral suspensions, injectables, ophthalmic ointments and solutions, ear solutions and suspensions, topical sprays, and gels, can be found here .
 The company reports having received 98 complaints thus far, 7 of which they classified as serious.
 Recall action steps
 To assist with the recall, Wedgewood is working with Sedgwick to notify affected customers and arrange for a refund or a replacement of recalled products where possible. Wedgewood is also working with pet owners, veterinarians, and other customers to identify clinically appropriate alternatives to affected compounded products where needed.
 Customers who have an affected product should stop using it and contact Wedgewood’s recall services at 866-562-5931, Monday through Friday, 8AM to 9 PM ET and Saturday 9AM to 5PM ET.
 Any suspected adverse reactions or quality concerns associated with an affected product should be reported to the FDA at 1-888-FDA-VETS or at www.FDA.gov/reportanimalae .
 Trends reached out to Wedgewood for comment but did not receive one as of publication time.
